title: The envelope is real
statement: Let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse Weil sheaf, punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$, and let $b\in\Qlb^\times$ satisfy $|\iota(b)|=q^{-w/2}$. Then the envelope $\operatorname{Env}_\iota(\mathcal F;b)$ of [def-wf-normalized-real-envelope] is $\iota$-real in the sense of [def-wf-iota-real]. Moreover, $\operatorname{Env}_\iota(\mathcal F;b)$ is lisse.

proof.text: By [lem-wf-constant-twist-weight], the normalized twist $\mathcal F^0=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal B_b$ has punctual weight $0$ under the displayed norm hypothesis (equivalently, this is the normalization in [def-wf-normalized-real-envelope]). At a closed point $y$, write $\beta_j$ for the eigenvalues of the Frobenius on $\mathcal F^0_{\bar y}$. Thus $|\iota(\beta_j)|=q_y^0=1$.

The sheaf $\mathcal F^0=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal B_b$ is lisse of finite rank, since $\mathcal F$ is and $\mathcal B_b$ of [def-wf-constant-weil-twist] is a rank-one lisse Weil sheaf (a tensor product of locally constant finite-rank sheaves is locally constant of finite rank). The second summand of the envelope is the linear dual of $\mathcal F^0$. By [lem-tw-dual-stalk-frobenius], applied to the lisse sheaf $\mathcal F^0$, its local Frobenius is the contragredient, and [p-linear-spectra] gives eigenvalues $\beta_j^{-1}$. Since $|\iota(\beta_j)|=1$, the elementary identity $z^{-1}=\overline z$ for $|z|=1$ gives $\iota(\beta_j^{-1})=\overline{\iota(\beta_j)}$. The local characteristic factor of the direct sum is the product of the two factors, so its eigenvalue multiset is stable under complex conjugation.
By the definition [def-wf-iota-real], conjugation stability of the local eigenvalue multiset at every closed point is exactly that $\operatorname{Env}_\iota(\mathcal F;b)$ is $\iota$-real.

Finally, $\mathcal F^0$ is lisse as noted in step 2, the dual of a lisse sheaf is lisse by [lem-tw-dual-stalk-frobenius], and a direct sum of lisse sheaves is lisse by the definition of local constancy. Therefore the envelope is lisse.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a Weil sheaf, punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$,
and let $b\in\Qlb^\times$ with $|\iota(b)|=q^{-w/2}$ (for instance
$b=\iota^{-1}(q^{-w/2})$). Then the envelope
$\operatorname{Env}_\iota(\mathcal F;b)$ of
[def-wf-normalized-real-envelope] is $\iota$-real in the sense of
[def-wf-iota-real]. If $\mathcal F$ is lisse, so is
$\operatorname{Env}_\iota(\mathcal F;b)$.

proof.text:
At a closed point $y$, the local characteristic factor of the
envelope is the product of the local factors of the two summands, with
eigenvalues $\beta_j$ (of $\mathcal F^0_{\bar y}$) and
$\beta_j^{-1}$ (of its dual), where
$|\iota(\beta_j)|=q_y^{0}=1$ by the normalization of
[def-wf-normalized-real-envelope] and the punctual purity of
weight $0$ of [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Hence

$$
\iota\bigl(\beta_j^{-1}\bigr)=\overline{\iota(\beta_j)}
$$

($\overline z=|z|^2z^{-1}=z^{-1}$ for $|z|=1$), so the local
eigenvalue multiset is stable under complex conjugation; by
[def-wf-iota-real] the envelope is $\iota$-real.

split_report.summary: Corrected the imported statement to the mathematically intended lisse hypothesis and added the lissity conclusion from the current blueprint. The original arbitrary-constructible reading is false: a Weil line on G_m with Frobenius i extended by zero has a missing-point dual eigenvalue -i, so its envelope need not be real. The proof now separates normalization to weight zero, the contragredient inverse-eigenvalue calculation, the definition of reality, and preservation of lissity. All cited facts are existing DAG nodes; no new nodes were needed.

The worker's counterexample checks out: F = j_!L on A^1, where L is a geometrically constant line on G_m with Frobenius i. Its dual j_*L^vee has Frobenius -i at the origin, while F has stalk 0 there.
